description: A stateful NAT64 of the router, an instance of Jool in a network namespace of its own that a link joins to its VRF: it translates IPv6 connections to addresses of its prefix into IPv4 connections to the address each embeds, from the addresses of its pool.

pool4.description: IPv4 addresses, with their ports, that the translated connections leave from: addresses routed to the router, not addresses of its links, which the router answers itself. The renderer refuses an address that a `Network` document gives a link. An address from DHCP passes unchecked but does not work either; leave pool4 empty instead. Empty takes the address of the link a connection leaves through, with the ports 61001 to 65535, which the router masquerades. The firewall's NAT rules leave the translated connections alone.

ports.description: Ports, or ICMP identifiers, of the addresses the translated connections take: a port or a range `<first>-<last>` that leaves out the kernel's ephemeral ports, 32768 to 60999, which the router's own connections take.

prefix.description: IPv4 addresses the translated connections leave from, a range of 65536 addresses at most.

protocols.description: Protocols whose connections take the addresses and ports.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A pool's entries are IPv4 ranges of 65536 addresses at most.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "the pool entry " + self.filter(a, !(cidr(a.prefix).ip(0).family() == "ipv4" && cidr(a.prefix).prefix() >= 16))[0].prefix + " is no IPv4 range of 16 bits or more"

x-chalkos-rules.description: A pool's entries hold no unspecified, loopback, multicast or broadcast address.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "the pool entry " + self.filter(a, !cel.bind(c, cidr(a.prefix), c.ip(0).family() != "ipv4" || c.ip(0) != ip("0.0.0.0") && !cidr("127.0.0.0/8").contains(c.ip(0)) && !cidr("224.0.0.0/4").contains(c.ip(0)) && !c.contains(ip("255.255.255.255"))))[0].prefix + " holds addresses no connection leaves from: the unspecified address, loopback, multicast or broadcast"
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(a, cel.bind(c, cidr(a.prefix), c.ip(0).family() != "ipv4" || c.ip(0) != ip("0.0.0.0") && !cidr("127.0.0.0/8").contains(c.ip(0)) && !cidr("224.0.0.0/4").contains(c.ip(0)) && !c.contains(ip("255.255.255.255"))))

x-chalkos-rules.description: A pool's entries hold no link-local address; the NAT64s' links take 169.254.64.0/18.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "the pool entry " + self.filter(a, cidr("169.254.0.0/16").contains(cidr(a.prefix).ip(0)))[0].prefix + " holds link-local addresses, which the NAT64s' links take"

x-chalkos-rules.description: A pool entry's ports lie from 1 to 65535 and leave out the kernel's ephemeral ports, 32768 to 60999.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "a pool entry takes the ports " + string(self.filter(a, !cel.bind(lo, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[0])), cel.bind(hi, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[1])), lo >= 1 && lo <= hi && hi <= 65535 && (hi < 32768 || lo > 60999))))[0].ports) + ", which lie outside 1-32767 and 61000-65535 or run backwards; Jool refuses the kernel's ephemeral ports, 32768 to 60999"
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self.all(a, cel.bind(lo, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[0])), cel.bind(hi, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[1])), lo >= 1 && lo <= hi && hi <= 65535 && (hi < 32768 || lo > 60999))))

x-chalkos-rules.description: A pool entry names each protocol once.
x-chalkos-rules.message: a pool entry names a protocol twice

x-chalkos-rules.description: No two entries of a pool share a protocol, addresses and ports.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(e, self.map(a, ["tcp", "udp", "icmp"].filter(p, p in a.protocols).map(p, [p, a.prefix, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[0])), (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[1]))])).flatten(), cel.bind(x, e.filter(x, size(e.filter(y, x[0] == y[0] && (cidr(x[1]).contains(cidr(y[1]).ip(0)) || cidr(y[1]).contains(cidr(x[1]).ip(0))) && x[2] <= y[3] && y[2] <= x[3])) > 1)[0], "the pool entry " + x[1] + " shares " + x[0] + " addresses and ports with another; give each entry of a protocol addresses or ports of its own"))
x-chalkos-rules.rule: cel.bind(e, self.map(a, ["tcp", "udp", "icmp"].filter(p, p in a.protocols).map(p, [p, a.prefix, (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[0])), (type(a.ports) == int ? a.ports : int(a.ports.split("-")[1]))])).flatten(), e.all(x, size(e.filter(y, x[0] == y[0] && (cidr(x[1]).contains(cidr(y[1]).ip(0)) || cidr(y[1]).contains(cidr(x[1]).ip(0))) && x[2] <= y[3] && y[2] <= x[3])) <= 1))

prefix.description: IPv6 range whose addresses the NAT64 translates, each embedding an IPv4 address as RFC 6052 says: 32, 40, 48, 56, 64 or 96 bits, by default the well-known prefix. The router routes it to the NAT64's link in the NAT64's VRF, a route that BGP announces when `BGP.spec.networks` of that VRF names the prefix.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A NAT64 prefix is an IPv6 range of 32, 40, 48, 56, 64 or 96 bits of no link-local, multicast or unspecified addresses, whose bits 64 to 71 are zero, as RFC 6052 gives them.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: !(cidr(self).ip(0).family() == "ipv6" && cidr(self).prefix() in [32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 96] && !cidr("::ffff:0:0/96").contains(cidr(self).ip(0))) ? "the prefix " + self + " is no NAT64 prefix; give an IPv6 range of 32, 40, 48, 56, 64 or 96 bits, such as 64:ff9b::/96" : !cel.bind(x, cidr(self).ip(0), x != ip("::") && !cidr("fe80::/10").contains(x) && !cidr("ff00::/8").contains(x)) ? "the prefix " + self + " holds link-local, multicast or unspecified addresses" : "the prefix " + self + " sets bits 64 to 71, which RFC 6052 keeps zero"
x-chalkos-rules.rule: cidr(self).ip(0).family() == "ipv6" && cidr(self).prefix() in [32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 96] && !cidr("::ffff:0:0/96").contains(cidr(self).ip(0)) && cel.bind(x, cidr(self).ip(0), x != ip("::") && !cidr("fe80::/10").contains(x) && !cidr("ff00::/8").contains(x)) && cel.bind(a, string(cidr(self).ip(0)), cidr(a + "/72").ip(0) == cidr(a + "/64").ip(0))

vrf.description: VRF document whose links route the prefix to the NAT64 and carry its translated connections; null for the default VRF. The NAT64 runs in the network namespace nat64-<name>, which the link n64-<name> joins to the VRF.

title: NAT64

rules.description: A NAT64's name has 11 characters at most, as its link n64-<name> is an interface's name of 15.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, size(n) > 11).map(n, "NAT64 " + n).join(", ") + " has a name of more than 11 characters, which its link n64-<name> does not take as an interface's name; give it a shorter one"

rules.description: A NAT64's vrf is a VRF document.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(vrfs, (("router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1" in config && "VRF" in config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"]) ? config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"].VRF : {}), documents.filter(n, documents[n].spec.vrf != null && !(documents[n].spec.vrf in vrfs)).map(n, "NAT64 " + n + " names the VRF " + documents[n].spec.vrf).join(", ") + ", which no VRF document declares; leave vrf out for the default VRF")
rules.rule: cel.bind(vrfs, (("router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1" in config && "VRF" in config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"]) ? config["router.chalkos.dev/v1alpha1"].VRF : {}), documents.all(n, documents[n].spec.vrf == null || documents[n].spec.vrf in vrfs))

rules.description: No two NAT64s of one VRF translate addresses of one prefix.
rules.messageExpression: documents.filter(n, documents.exists(m, n != m && (documents[n].spec.vrf == null ? "default" : documents[n].spec.vrf) == (documents[m].spec.vrf == null ? "default" : documents[m].spec.vrf) && (cidr(documents[n].spec.prefix).contains(cidr(documents[m].spec.prefix).ip(0)) || cidr(documents[m].spec.prefix).contains(cidr(documents[n].spec.prefix).ip(0))))).map(n, "NAT64 " + n).join(", ") + " translate addresses of one prefix in one VRF; give each NAT64 of a VRF a prefix of its own"
rules.rule: documents.all(n, documents.all(m, n == m || (documents[n].spec.vrf == null ? "default" : documents[n].spec.vrf) != (documents[m].spec.vrf == null ? "default" : documents[m].spec.vrf) || !(cidr(documents[n].spec.prefix).contains(cidr(documents[m].spec.prefix).ip(0)) || cidr(documents[m].spec.prefix).contains(cidr(documents[n].spec.prefix).ip(0)))))

rules.description: No two NAT64s share an address of their pools.
rules.messageExpression: cel.bind(e, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.pool4.map(a, [n, a.prefix])).flatten(), e.filter(x, e.exists(y, x[0] != y[0] && (cidr(x[1]).contains(cidr(y[1]).ip(0)) || cidr(y[1]).contains(cidr(x[1]).ip(0))))).map(x, "NAT64 " + x[0] + " " + x[1]).join(", ") + " share addresses; give each NAT64 a pool of its own")
rules.rule: cel.bind(e, documents.map(n, documents[n].spec.pool4.map(a, [n, a.prefix])).flatten(), e.all(x, e.all(y, x[0] == y[0] || !(cidr(x[1]).contains(cidr(y[1]).ip(0)) || cidr(y[1]).contains(cidr(x[1]).ip(0))))))
